text:
maria: Quick question — we're wiring Cloud KMS for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem connector). Need clarity on which service account needs which IAM roles, keyring placement, envelope encryption pattern, and a safe rotation flow. Low-ops but auditable.

sam: Start simple: create a dedicated SA (e.g. redwood-private-kms-sa@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com). Grant it roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the specific CryptoKey (not project-wide). Avoid broad roles. :thumbsup:

jess: Checklist I usually follow:
- Key ring in same region as the runtime to avoid egress (or multi-region if you need HA)
- Grant roles at the CryptoKey level (cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter)
- Enable Cloud Audit Logs (Data Access) for KMS and export to our SIEM/BigQuery
- Use envelope encryption: generate DEK per object, wrap with KMS, store wrapped key alongside ciphertext
- Rotation via key versions + background rewrap job (not manual).

noah: Example commands we can use in infra (replace PROJECT and locations):
```
# create key ring
gcloud kms keyrings create redwood-keyring --location=us-central1 --project=PROJECT

# create symmetric key (purpose=encryption)
gcloud kms keys create redwood-data-key --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-keyring --purpose=encryption

# grant encrypt/decrypt to the SA
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding redwood-data-key --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-keyring \
  --member=serviceAccount:redwood-private-kms-sa@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter

# set automatic rotation (example: 30d)
gcloud kms keys update redwood-data-key --location=us-central1 --keyring=redwood-keyring \
  --rotation-period=2592000s --next-rotation-time=\"2026-04-01T00:00:00Z\"
```

maria: For envelope encryption, where do we store DEKs (plaintext)? We shouldn't persist plaintext anywhere.

jess: Right — never persist plaintext DEKs. Typical flow:
1) At object write: generate a random DEK locally in the Private runtime, encrypt data with DEK, call KMS encrypt on the DEK (KMS returns wrapped_key), store wrapped_key + ciphertext
2) At read: fetch wrapped_key, call KMS decrypt to get DEK, decrypt data in-memory.

For rotation (when primary key version changes): run a rewrap job that for each wrapped_key does: call KMS decrypt (old primary is still usable) to get DEK plaintext, then call KMS encrypt with the new primary to produce a new wrapped_key, store it and delete/mark old wrapped_key rotated. Keep this job minimal-privilege and rate-limited. :gear:

sam: A few permission notes:
- Grant the SA only roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the key(s).
- If you want the control plane to impersonate a short-lived SA instead of giving it direct access, give control-plane-sa roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator on redwood-private-kms-sa. That way the control plane can get a token and act as the kms-sa (favours centralized audit).

noah: On audit logging and compliance:
- Enable KMS Data Access logs (they're disabled by default in some orgs). Those logs capture Encrypt/Decrypt/AsymmetricSign etc.
- Export logs to a dedicated project or BigQuery table for retention and alerting (suspicious decrypt spikes, cross-region decrypts).
- Add a log-based alert for "decrypts by more than X per minute" or decrypts outside business hours.

maria: What about key ring vs multi-region key selection? We want low latency but also DR.

jess: If Private runtime lives in a single region, put key ring in same region. If you need failover across regions, use a multi-region key ring or a second key ring + replication plan and accept cross-region egress. Document the DR failover runbook.

maria: Who should be able to create new key versions / rotate? Ops only? Product?

sam: Principle: separate duties. Only an ops/infra role (human + automation) should have roles/cloudkms.admin or roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersionManager. Application SAs should only have encrypt/decrypt. Rotation can be automated by an ops-owned job (or Cloud Scheduler + Cloud Function) that has the required role. Store rotation schedule in Terraform/infra-as-code.

noah: Quick Terraform note: manage CryptoKey IAM at the key level (google_kms_crypto_key_iam_binding) so we don't accidentally open up the project. Also add lifecycle rules to prevent accidental deletions.

maria: Any gotchas for Private (air-gapped / VPC) setups?

jess: For on-prem or VPC Private deployments where outbound to GCP is restricted: you still need network egress to call KMS unless you use a proxy. Options:
- Allow egress to kms.googleapis.com with limited VPC egress rules
- Run a small, authenticated proxy in a permitted network that forwards to KMS (service account + mTLS)
- Pre-warm and cache wrapped DEKs carefully if you must avoid frequent KMS calls (dangerous for rotation/audit).

maria: OK this is great. Can someone drop a short PR template for the infra change (IAM + key creation) so I can review?

noah: I'll open a draft Terraform PR with keyring/key + IAM bindings + a log sink in the next hour, pinging infra squad. :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: terraform plan created for //infra/kms/redwood-keyring (run-12345) — review at https://our-terraform.example/runs/12345

maria: Thanks all — saved me from three different wrong ways to do this. I'll link the PR to the compliance ticket and we can schedule the rotation runbook review. :rocket:
